summary: Leadership is room-specific. In #best Claude Opus 4.7 is the only agent with a positive assignment net (16 sent, 8 received), leads 11-14 May and gets its plans claimed within minutes, but 16 of its 29 real task links restate work already under way. #rest has no stable leader: the top assigner changes daily, its titles (study lead GPT-5.4, coordinator Opus 4.6) are protocol roles, and approvals and accepted corrections go to the checker GPT-5.4 (GPT-5.5 in #best); assignments are acted on in 170 of 198 real links, yet only 86 (43%) start after the message.

questions.question: Who assigns tasks to whom, per room and per day, and what is each agent's net (assigned minus received)? Use the stored `delegation` labels (L.labels, rubric 'delegation', label 'directs'; a blind check agreed on 37 of 40), resolve addressees from the mention table AND short names in the text. Per-agent net; top assigner per room per day.
questions.answer: 110 'directs' messages, 227 addressee links (13 from short names only). Only Claude Opus 4.7 has a positive net (+8: 16 sent, 8 received, all from Gemini 3.1 Pro; it directs GPT-5.5 13, Gemini 12, Kimi 6); every #rest agent is net negative, DeepSeek-V3.2 sends most (19) but receives 27.
questions.precision: addressee links 21 of 25 (seed 41); full hand reading in L6 found 29 of 227 links carry no task; labels: stored blind check 37 of 40
questions.limits: Received counts include agents only @-listed in broadcast posts (about 13%), and plans posted without an @-mention carry no label.

questions.question: Whose proposed plans get adopted, meaning others claim their items within 10 minutes? Plan-like messages (numbered items, "proposal", "plan:") followed by "I'll take / on it / claiming" replies; per-agent plans proposed and adopted.
questions.answer: Of 85 plan-pattern messages 53 are real plans (hand); of 32 claim-pattern replies 11 claim an item of another agent's proposal within 10 min, crediting 8 proposals. Claude Opus 4.7 has 3 proposals adopted by 6 claims (every #best room-mate); DeepSeek-V3.2 posts the most plans (25) but only 2 are claimed.
questions.precision: plan pattern 17 of 25 and claim-to-plan pairing 7 of 15, both below 80%: all 85 plan matches and all 32 claim matches read by hand
questions.limits: Adopted proposals include 3 the plan pattern missed (Opus 4.7, Opus 4.5, GPT-5.4), and claims worded otherwise ('I accept', 'count me in') are not found.

questions.question: Whom do agents ask for permission or approval ("can I", "should I", "OK to", "go ahead?", "approve")? The approval authority per room.
questions.answer: 22 permission requests (15 #rest, 7 #best). #rest authority is GPT-5.4 (asked 5 times by name, gave 3 approvals) with GPT-5.2 approving DeepSeek (2); DeepSeek-V3.2 asks most (6) and 6 #rest requests got no answer. #best has no approver: Opus 4.7 asks (4) more than it is asked (2) and answers are spread over all four.
questions.precision: all 24 matches read by hand: 22 of 24 are requests; who answered read by hand (the program's yes-detector was 7 of 18)
questions.limits: Only question-form requests with the listed phrases are found; 9 of 22 are addressed to the whole room.

questions.question: Whose corrections are accepted ("you're right", "good catch", followed by a fix)? Per-agent corrections accepted.
questions.answer: 56 concession messages; corrector resolved for 50. The checkers dominate: GPT-5.4 15 (#rest), GPT-5.5 8 (#best), then Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 6 each; the #best lead Opus 4.7 has 4, DeepSeek-V3.2 0. Conceders: DeepSeek 11, Opus 4.5 10, Opus 4.6 10, Gemini 3.1 Pro 9.
questions.precision: 20 of 25 (seed 41), after fixing attribution (v1 crediting every addressee was 15 of 25)
questions.limits: The 'followed by a fix' test (own fix message or write action within 30 min) fires on 55 of 56, so it does not discriminate and is not reported separately.

questions.question: Does leadership rotate? L1 per day per room: the top agent per day; did it change?
questions.answer: #best: no; Opus 4.7 tops 11-14 May (6, 4, 5, 1 of 8, 6, 8, 1) and only on 15 May does Gemini 3.1 Pro send the room's single assignment. #rest: yes, the top changes every day: DeepSeek-V3.2 and Opus 4.5 tie (8 each of 33), Opus 4.6 (10 of 15), Haiku 4.5 (4 of 11), DeepSeek (7 of 21), GPT-5.2 and Haiku tie (2 of 6).
questions.precision: as L1 (labels 37 of 40; senders need no addressee resolution)
questions.limits: Counts are small after 13 May in #best (1 a day), so 'top' there means little.

questions.question: Are assignments carried out, and does the addressee act after the message rather than before? For each `directs` message, the addressee's actions or messages in the next 30 minutes compared with the task, excluding work already started before the message (check by program where possible, read a sample to validate); per-assigner rate done.
questions.answer: Of 227 links, 29 carry no task; of the 198 real ones 86 (43%) were done after the message, 84 (42%) were already under way or started within 15 s, 6 declined, 16 did other work, 6 absent. Done-after rate: Opus 4.5 72%, Opus 4.6 57%, GPT-5.4 50%, Haiku 40%, DeepSeek 32%, Opus 4.7 28% (16 of its 29 restate work already started).
questions.precision: keyword program 4 of 25 (seed 41), so all 227 links read by hand; a second reader agreed on 22 of 25
questions.limits: Evidence shows chat and shell-action intents, not GUI clicks, so screen-only work (Kimi, GPT-5) can look idle; 'started before' looks back 10 min.

questions.question: Who claims a leadership title ("lead", "coordinator", "manager", "PI") for itself, and do others call it that? Per agent: claimed vs recognised.
questions.answer: 46 title matches, 29 apply to goal-41 agents (37 attributions), none in #best. Recognised leaders: Claude Opus 4.6 (2 self 'coordinator', 8 uses by 4 others) and GPT-5.4 (2 self 'study lead', 7 by 2 others); Haiku 4.5 (2 self) and DeepSeek-V3.2 (3 self, in closing posts) are titled mainly by each other.
questions.precision: all 46 read by hand (automatic attribution agreed on 35 of 46)
questions.limits: Sonnet 4.5's 4 are the phrase 'scorer/coordinator only' for an exposure rule, not a leadership role; no 'PI' and only one historical 'manager' occur.
